workstream: U23 -- bounded diagnostic comparison (NOT a training run): why does PPO training move away from the zero-action standing baseline, even at stage 0?
motivation: U22's curriculum never advanced past stage 0 (pure balance, desired_vx=0.0) across an 800k-step budget, despite zero forward-velocity demand. Explicit instruction: investigate action scaling and exploration next, using the known zero-action standing policy as the control -- and do NOT extend the training budget yet.
method: Four controllers under identical resets (CaraWalkEnv.reset() is confirmed fully deterministic -- no noise added to the keyframe pose -- so this is automatically satisfied), identical stage-0 reward (desired_vx=0.0), identical episode length (200 steps / 4s), identical model config (the same cara_full_body.yaml dynamic MJCF used everywhere in this project). Observation normalizer held frozen during every rollout (no online updates), to isolate policy behavior from a shifting normalizer.

action_range_translation.note: left/right symmetric. hip_pitch has the largest range (24 deg), ankle_roll the smallest (7.6 deg).

exploration_std_translation.note: The initial exploration std alone predicts that at least one of the 12 joints' sampled action exceeds the [-1,1] action bound on ~72% of steps, before any training happens. This was a theoretical check computed BEFORE the empirical rollout confirmed it.

1_zero_action.note: Reconfirms standing under the actual training resets/config -- holds full 200-step episode.

2_untrained_mean.note: The freshly-initialized policy's MEAN output is nearly zero (orthogonal init with std=0.01 on the final actor layer) -- initialization starts almost exactly at the zero-action standing baseline, matching it within 1.2 return points.

3_untrained_sampled.note: Sampling noise ALONE, from the SAME mean policy that stood perfectly in condition 2, destroys stance in 21 steps on average across all 10 independent repeats -- a 100% fall rate. This mean_steps=21.3 also closely matches what real PPO training showed throughout U21 and most of U22 (~20-30 steps).

4_trained_mean.note: After 800k steps of training against overwhelmingly falling (noise-corrupted) rollouts, the DETERMINISTIC mean policy itself has been pulled away from its good initialization -- it no longer resembles the near-zero mean of condition 2, and its return (-18.23) is now worse than the untrained mean's (191.82).

decision_sequence_readout.step1_zero_action_fails_under_training_r: NO -- zero action holds the full episode (193.00 return). Reset/baseline stability is confirmed fine.
decision_sequence_readout.step2_zero_action_rewarded_poorly: NO -- zero-action return (193.00) is far ABOVE the trained/learned-fall return (-18.23). The objective correctly favors standing; this is not a reward problem.
decision_sequence_readout.step3_initial_mean_succeeds_sampling_fai: YES -- untrained mean stands (191.82, matches zero action), untrained SAMPLED falls 100% of the time (mean 21.3 steps). This is the branch that fired.
decision_sequence_readout.conclusion: Per the given decision rule: reduce initial exploration std first, keeping the action bounds (action_range_frac=0.30) unchanged. Steps 4 (actuator path) and 5 (PPO updates/obs normalization) were not reached -- their preconditions were not met by this evidence.

not_done_this_turn: No training budget was spent or extended, per instruction. No fix has been implemented or validated yet -- this run is diagnosis only. The concrete next step (lower initial actor_logstd, e.g. via a new --init-logstd CLI flag on train_ppo.py, keeping action_range_frac=0.30 unchanged, then a bounded validation run at the SAME budget scale as U21/U22) is proposed but not started, pending confirmation.
